headline: Margins rebound sharply as AI server demand accelerates
summary_short: Supermicro's Q4 FY2026 net sales rose 93.2% y/y (+8.6% q/q) to $11.12 billion as GAAP gross margin rebounded to 17.5% from 9.5% a year ago, lifting diluted EPS to $1.62 (+422.6% y/y); the company guided FY2027 net sales of $65.0-$72.0 billion.
summary_long: Net sales rose 93.2% y/y and 8.6% q/q to $11.12 billion, with GAAP gross margin rebounding to 17.5% from 9.5% a year ago on a richer enterprise mix and broader DCBBS adoption, per CEO Charles Liang. Diluted EPS rose to $1.62 GAAP (+422.6% y/y) and $1.70 non-GAAP. Full fiscal 2026 net sales grew 77.8% to $39.1 billion, though full-year gross margin slipped to 10.8% from 11.1% on weaker first-half quarters. Cash rose to $7.5 billion while bank debt and convertible notes rose 83.3% to $8.7 billion; full-year operating cash flow swung to a $6.8 billion use as inventory and receivables grew sharply. Guidance: Q1 FY2027 net sales $14.5-$15.5 billion; FY2027 net sales $65.0-$72.0 billion.

drivers.explanation: Management attributes the rebound to accelerating AI/IT infrastructure demand, a richer mix of large enterprise customers, wider adoption of the company's DCBBS server architecture, over $60 billion of new orders added over the year, and record backlog entering fiscal 2027.
